section_name: Educational and Foundational Support for Teaching Residuals and Prediction Error

candidates.title: Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Pedagogical overview of regression without an intercept and its evaluation statistics. Directly relevant to explaining the omitted constant in the supplied baseline. [Teaching Statistics](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9639.00136).

candidates.title: The Examination and Analysis of Residuals
candidates.reason: Foundational overview of numerical and graphical residual analysis. Provides methodological grounding for interpreting the constant residual pattern as a systematic discrepancy between observations and predictions. [Technometrics](https://doi.org/10.1080/00401706.1963.10490071).

candidates.title: Root-mean-square error (RMSE) or mean absolute error (MAE): when to use them or not
candidates.reason: Review and perspective explaining error metrics and their interpretation. Relevant to distinguishing signed residuals from aggregated absolute or squared errors in the finite example. [Geoscientific Model Development](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/15/5481/2022/).

candidates.title: Another look at measures of forecast accuracy
candidates.reason: Highly influential comparative examination of accuracy measures and their limitations. Supports explicitly identifying the metric and aggregation used when reporting the example's error. [International Journal of Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001).

candidates.title: How Students Learn Statistics Revisited: A Current Review of Research on Teaching and Learning Statistics
candidates.reason: Broad review of statistical learning and instructional principles. Provides educational grounding for a concept-focused example connecting predictions, observations, residuals, and error calculations. [International Statistical Review](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1751-5823.2007.00029.x).

candidates.title: Learning from Examples: Instructional Principles from the Worked Examples Research
candidates.reason: Foundational review of worked-example instruction. Its principles are relevant to presenting the baseline predictions, residual calculations, and constant correction as explicit, connected steps. [Review of Educational Research](https://doi.org/10.3102/00346543070002181).

candidates.title: A Meta-analysis of the Worked Examples Effect on Mathematics Performance
candidates.reason: Meta-analysis synthesizing evidence on worked examples in mathematics. Supports the general educational motivation for transparent numerical demonstrations without establishing the effectiveness of this particular five-observation example. [Educational Psychology Review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09745-1).

candidates.title: How Effective are Instructional Explanations in Example-Based Learning? A Meta-Analytic Review
candidates.reason: Reviews 21 experiments and finds limited overall benefits from added explanations, with greater benefits for conceptual knowledge. Relevant to carefully explaining why the omitted offset produces identical residuals. [Educational Psychology Review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-010-9136-5).

candidates.title: Toward an Instructionally Oriented Theory of Example-Based Learning
candidates.reason: Influential theoretical synthesis integrating worked examples, observational learning, and analogical reasoning. Offers instructional principles applicable to making each arithmetic step and its underlying meaning explicit. [Cognitive Science](https://doi.org/10.1111/cogs.12086).

candidates.title: Conditions for Effective Learning from Erroneous Examples: A Systematic Review
candidates.reason: Systematic review of 40 studies examining explanations, correction activities, and learner characteristics. Relevant to designing a demonstration that identifies an omitted offset and explains its correction; benefits depend on instructional conditions. [Educational Psychology Review](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-025-10071-x).
